hypothesis: Coalesced contiguous-K BF16 loads plus 65-column threadgroup transpose reduce global transaction dispersion/bank conflicts for existing 16x64x64 and 32x64x32 FP32 MMA tiles. Same values, K reduction order and original decode path.
tradeoffs: Extra 256/128 bytes of shared memory per wide tile; transpose stores and SIMD stride may cost latency. No extra model weight copies. Small-row/small-output fallback unchanged.
sequence: After WS-M5-03 terminal: correctness tests then fresh WorldSense ABBA on unchanged cases. Fresh confirmation only on pass. No performance timing outside WorldSense.

scheduling_amendment_before_any_performa.reason: Prior process-level comparisons show large drift; isolate dispatcher in the same loaded binary and WorldSense process. Actual counters distinguish disabled vs enabled and prove decode untouched.
scheduling_amendment_before_any_performa.worker_1: Warm A/B windows then ABBA windows, same three fixed cases/query per window; two measured repeats per policy
scheduling_amendment_before_any_performa.worker_2: Fresh process, warm B/A then BAAB; prospective confirmation if initial screen passes
scheduling_amendment_before_any_performa.scope: Same native binary, model weights, contexts, prompts, compiler and pipeline. Policy restored after every call, including inference exception. All model calls still pass through WorldSense/Galaxy.
scheduling_amendment_before_any_performa.selection: Both fresh workers must pass unchanged performance gates and all output/route/state checks. No retrospective selection of favorable windows.
